test: explains a historical Archive Project acknowledgement and does not retry it
evidence: Archive's browser command wrapper must propagate historical acknowledgement unavailability after exactly one PUT/Challenge instead of entering its own automatic retry. Other command wrappers have separate catch/retry bodies, and real HTTP historical evidence tests call the generated client directly. Despite its title this case does not mount a UI or verify explanatory text; retain only the no-retry/protocol-classification claim.

test: explains a historical Update Project acknowledgement and does not retry it
evidence: Project rename must show the historical explanation while retaining the author's unsaved title and the listed Project, with exactly one command and Challenge. Volume/Chapter rename use different React components and wrapper functions; real HTTP proves the error response but not form preservation or command resubmission.

test: explains a historical Create Volume acknowledgement and does not retry it
evidence: Create Volume must render its historical error in the inline form without retrying the POST or allocating another Challenge. Create Chapter has a different wrapper/form component and error state; server structural replay coverage does not execute either browser catch path.

test: keeps the pending inline title when another creation is requested and explains the historical acknowledgement
evidence: A held Chapter creation must keep the original connected read-only input, title and target Volume when another creation is requested; after historical failure it must show the specific error and send only the original POST/Challenge. Create Volume and completed creation journeys do not force this pending-form interleaving.

test: explains a historical Delete Volume acknowledgement and does not retry it
evidence: Confirmed Volume deletion must display the historical acknowledgement alert and avoid the delete-volume wrapper's automatic retry. Chapter deletion has its own wrapper and view handler. This case checks the Project title but does not explicitly assert that the Volume row remains.

test: explains a historical Delete Chapter acknowledgement and does not retry it
evidence: Confirmed Chapter deletion must preserve its visible Chapter and show the historical alert after exactly one DELETE/Challenge. Volume deletion executes different command and view catch paths; HTTP only establishes the received problem, not whether the browser removes the item or retries it.

test: explains a historical Update Volume acknowledgement and does not retry it
evidence: Volume rename must keep the typed title and show its historical error without a second PATCH or Challenge. Its volume-tree-actions component and update-volume retry wrapper are independent of the Project and Chapter forms; server-side shared structural replay cannot observe discarded form text.

test: explains a historical Update Chapter acknowledgement and does not retry it
evidence: Chapter rename must retain the author's input and surrounding Volume while presenting the historical error after one PATCH/Challenge. Updating a Volume uses a separate component and wrapper; successful packaged rename does not execute this catch branch.

test: explains a historical Set Current Chapter acknowledgement and does not retry it
evidence: Requesting another Current Chapter and receiving historical unavailability must leave Chapter A displayed, show the alert and make only one PUT. This guards the switch recovery state plus set-current-chapter's own retry guard; rename/delete error forms do not execute navigation state changes.

test: explains a historical Undo Latest Author Action acknowledgement and does not retry it
evidence: The editor Undo shortcut must report historical unavailability while retaining saved state and no editor failure, with one Undo POST. Undo's command catch and editor-state cleanup differ from structural form errors; real Undo historical replay does not dispatch a keyboard event or inspect browser failure state.

test: explains a historical human-readable export acknowledgement and does not retry it
evidence: The readable export control must display historical unavailability and retain the visible Chapter after one admission POST. Its export-human-readable retry map and manuscript-readable-export error state are separate from rename/navigation; HTTP historical evidence cannot prove this button state or avoid browser retry.

test: keeps the generated outcome Query proof header-only
evidence: The executed generated outcome client must require proof and send it only in the anti-forgery header on an exact bodyless GET with same-origin credentials. Server tests exercise actual protected outcomes but do not reject an extra proof copy in the URL; static OpenAPI/schema shape does not execute the browser request construction.

test: retries the same protected Acceptance after an unknown delivery
evidence: Acceptance delivery must retain exact body/key/nonce across unknown and unreadable responses, recover a persisted in-flight Attempt, and refuse a competing decision. A terminal challenge problem must clear unresolved status while a 401 after earlier unknown delivery remains unresolved; known 403 must block further automatic submission. Real HTTP Acceptance tests do not run IndexedDB transport classification. Receive the valid-flight pending-projection checks from acceptance-journal before removing that direct helper case.

test: rejects a foreign Acceptance flight before it can disappear from Journal recovery
evidence: Move the valid flight's one intent/group, sequence and needs_attention/unsettled-count assertions into the first unresolved stage of the public Acceptance delivery case. Its createFlight callers construct key, partition and frozen command fields from the same workspace; this test's hidden key and foreign flight argument are fabricated internal tuples, not stored-partition drift. Do not keep those negative inputs as proof of realistic recovery corruption. Preserve the useful public pending-projection observations before deleting this fixture.

test: uses typed input, clipboard, and Client Session commands in Google Chrome
evidence: Trusted insertion, IME and clipboard behavior already execute through the packaged manuscript input journey using the same commands. The cookie set action is used only by this foundation test; real journeys establish sessions another way and use this command only to clear them. Its foundation-cookie probe, result-kind literals and Chrome user-agent text add no independent product regression. The named journey covers actual editing, not a mutation confined to the unused cookie-set helper branch.

test: refuses navigation and code inputs at the production command boundary
evidence: Move the five malformed/unsupported/extra-field production command inputs into a Node contract test for parseProductionHostRequest (proposed node-contract/browser-command-contract.test.ts). This exact-object validator is called at the privileged browser-command dispatch boundary, but the test invokes a pure parser with no browser or transport. Existing successful production journeys cannot prove rejection of arbitrary navigation/code inputs; preserve the guard coverage in the cheaper owning layer.

test: opens a listed empty Project from getProject, not from the list payload
evidence: Opening an empty Project must replace a stale/different library title with getProject's current title and load the canonical empty tree. The packaged library test uses matching list/query titles and cannot detect reusing the stale list payload as the opened Project. This test requires the actual query plus visible replacement.

test: selects a tree Chapter through getChapter and keeps pending on the current Chapter
evidence: Read-only inspection of another Chapter must leave the current Chapter's unsent text intact; returning must show that pending text, and a later expired Chapter query must keep it while showing a user-facing error without raw protocol text. Packaged navigation opens empty Chapters and does not combine a pending edit with failed inspection. Local current_chapter override rejection is overlapping coverage, not the unique reason.

test: opens the URL-selected Project and fails closed before invalid entry requests
evidence: Entry must use the URL Project rather than stale document metadata, and malformed/extra-segment Project URLs must render a blocked state without any request or stale page content. The Node Project opener receives an already selected ID; library opening has a valid ID and no invalid URL. Keep these entry/DOM cases; the normal query order/credentials and protected-home wording repeat other owners.

A 429 Challenge must leave the Author Edit saving without failure, then submit the same frozen group/key after the seven-second scheduled delay and reach the exact saved projection. Author Undo uses the shared wait helper but a different consumer, group creation and projection installation path; real server rate tests cannot prove browser retention/retry identity.
test: keeps an Author Edit saving through a Challenge rate limit and retries the same group

evidence: Closing the Author Edit idle controller during Retry-After must clear its timer, resolve idle and issue no second Challenge. Undo teardown invokes a separate controller/cancel path; successful delayed submission cannot detect a stuck idle promise or retry after this controller closes.
test: ends a Challenge rate-limit wait when the editor closes

evidence: Undo rate waiting must keep the mounted editor editable with saving state, make no Undo POST before retry, then send exactly one Undo with the same Challenge key and return to saved. Author Edit retries operate on a submission group rather than Undo's frontier and keyboard lifecycle. Receive duplicate-shortcut assertions before and during the wait from :164.
test: keeps the editor editable while an Author Undo waits for Challenge admission and retries the same Undo

evidence: Transfer the second Ctrl/Cmd+Z while the first Challenge is held and again during Retry-After into the successful Undo rate-limit case. Require one Challenge and one retry timer before releasing its existing successful path. This is the same fixture/Undo consumer and can verify exclusion plus eventual completion together; do not remove the repeated-key assertions before transfer.
test: ignores another Ctrl/Cmd+Z while an Author Undo is in progress

evidence: New trusted input during an Undo Retry-After wait must abandon that Undo, clear the timer and send no Undo request. Unmount uses effect cleanup rather than the input callback; late successful Challenge coverage starts before a timer exists and cannot prove cancellation of an already scheduled wait.
test: abandons an Author Undo Challenge wait at the editor input boundary

evidence: Unmount during Undo Retry-After must clear its timer and prevent an Undo request with no failure callback. Input cancellation uses a different trigger; Draft Undo teardown holds a source GET rather than a live Challenge timer and does not measure this scheduled-wait cleanup.
test: abandons an Author Undo Challenge wait at the editor unmount boundary

evidence: If the Undo POST is already in flight, new text must survive the delayed successful Undo response, Session refresh and queued Journal work. Cancelling a pre-admission wait sends no Undo POST, so it cannot detect late base installation clobbering new input.
test: keeps new input when the author types while the retried Author Undo request is in flight

evidence: Composition that abandons Undo while a successful Challenge response is held must prevent the subsequent Undo POST after response release. Existing Retry-After cancellation occurs after 429; the delayed-Undo-response case already submitted the command. This specifically checks currency after Challenge acquisition and before command submission.
test: does not send an abandoned Author Undo when its Challenge request completes after new input

evidence: Replacing the workspace while a Challenge is in flight must ignore its later 429 without scheduling a wait or publishing saving, and immediately accept the next Undo shortcut. Existing scheduled-wait cancellation cannot prove the post-cancel error continuation or release of the in-progress latch.
test: starts no Retry-After wait for an abandoned Author Undo and accepts the next Ctrl/Cmd+Z at once

evidence: Out-of-order sequence 2 must be held until sequence 1 arrives; repeated/reversed duplicate frames must converge to one ordered durable event set without changing pending prose. SSE consumption tests return ordered single frames and never force the held-gap buffer. The fresh in-order comparison confirms equivalent final ingest, not a measured performance property.
test: converges duplicate and reordered Activity frames to one durable ingest

evidence: The retained SSE consumer drives the same resyncProjectActivityFromSnapshot implementation with generation 1/position 1, a generation 2/position 5 Snapshot and a sequence-6 event, then requires the same durable ingest and unchanged full Journal. The direct helper's no-Activity-request count describes its internal step; the public consumer intentionally resumes Activity afterward. Unchanged Journal retains the same pending projection inputs.
test: preserves local payload and resumes after a new Snapshot generation

evidence: A same-Session Takeover winner with a higher generation must install a new partition, fence the old one, preserve all old journal evidence and reject writes through the old workspace. Fresh input must use the new base with a continuing local sequence and survive reload; generation downgrade must refuse without writes. Other-Session recovery reconstructs older bindings through a different branch.
test: resumes a Takeover winner without rebinding old journal evidence: valid

evidence: A winning different Editor Session must fence the older Session without rebinding its retained client binding/profile/base. Same-Session recovery computes the old expected partition from the new Session instead, so it cannot catch use of the winner's binding for a different Session. New input, reload and generation downgrade remain checked.
test: resumes a Takeover winner without rebinding old journal evidence: valid_other_session

evidence: A canonical query/Chapter position later than the winner's base must be accepted and initialize ingest at that later position, then reload the same partition. The two full winner journeys set canonical and base position equal, so they cannot detect an incorrect equality requirement. This early-return variant does not run their full old-evidence/new-input checks.
test: resumes a Takeover winner without rebinding old journal evidence: valid_activity_advance

evidence: A resumed Session claiming another Project Scope must not install a writable partition or alter any stored row. Valid winner tests do not inject a mismatched response scope; tree-locator scope is a later, separate response.
test: resumes a Takeover winner without rebinding old journal evidence: scope

evidence: A tree locator for another Project must prevent winner installation while preserving every old journal store. Session-scope and returned-Snapshot-ID faults affect other responses; ordinary Activity resync has a separate locator guard.
test: resumes a Takeover winner without rebinding old journal evidence: locator_scope

evidence: A resumed Session response with an identity different from the requested active Session must stay read-only without local writes. The valid other-Session case deliberately updates the active locator to match its response, so it does not exercise identity substitution.
test: resumes a Takeover winner without rebinding old journal evidence: session

evidence: A noncanonical writer generation '03' must not be installed as a new writer partition even though BigInt can parse it. Valid greater/lower generations contain canonical decimal strings; malformed canonical Snapshot position is another field and has an additional masking mismatch.
test: resumes a Takeover winner without rebinding old journal evidence: generation

evidence: Changed client Session binding for the same retained Editor Session must not relabel old journal evidence. Both valid winner cases keep the appropriate immutable old binding; generic transport scope refusal cannot prove retained-partition comparison.
test: resumes a Takeover winner without rebinding old journal evidence: binding

evidence: A higher writer generation must not reuse the old journal's base Snapshot identity while claiming a later activity position. Valid winner cases mint a new base ID; scope/digest checks permit this internally consistent response and cannot replace the retained-base comparison.
test: resumes a Takeover winner without rebinding old journal evidence: reused_base

evidence: A Session base with a false materialized-payload digest must not enter a writable workspace or change stored rows. The Snapshot locator and identity remain valid here; those faults do not exercise content verification.
test: resumes a Takeover winner without rebinding old journal evidence: digest

evidence: A getSnapshot result with another Snapshot identity than its locator must not install the winner even when the Project and positions match. Locator-scope coverage changes another response; position mismatch keeps the requested identity.
test: resumes a Takeover winner without rebinding old journal evidence: snapshot

evidence: Canonical position 4 is below base 5 but also differs from Chapter position 5. The equality-to-Chapter guard still rejects this input if the intended lower-bound guard is removed. The retained position_after_chapter case proves the same observed mismatch; this is not independent proof of the lower bound. A discriminating lower-bound case would need canonical and Chapter both below the base.
test: resumes a Takeover winner without rebinding old journal evidence: position_before_base

evidence: A canonical Snapshot at position 6 while the loaded Chapter is at 5 must not install a mixed-generation writable view. Valid activity advance sets both to 6; reused base changes identity instead. This is the retained owner for mismatched canonical/Chapter positions.
test: resumes a Takeover winner without rebinding old journal evidence: position_after_chapter

evidence: The oversized canonical position also differs from the Chapter position. Removing bounded-u64 validation can still yield read-only recovery at that mismatch, so this oracle does not isolate overflow refusal. The retained position_after_chapter case owns the observable mismatch. Do not claim it kills a mutation confined to the numeric validator.
test: resumes a Takeover winner without rebinding old journal evidence: position_invalid

evidence: An expired canonical Snapshot must prevent the atomic ingest/partition installation and leave all old stores unchanged. Identity and position are otherwise correct, so mismatch tests do not cover the expiry check in stageProjectActivitySnapshot.
test: resumes a Takeover winner without rebinding old journal evidence: expired

evidence: If the Session changes generation/base between the first read and the post-Snapshot recheck, winner installation must refuse with no local writes. All other invalid inputs are stable across both reads and cannot detect removal of that recheck.
test: resumes a Takeover winner without rebinding old journal evidence: drift

evidence: SSE consumption must persist Last-Event-ID, return idle without losing it, then replace an expired cursor using an owned Snapshot and resume the new generation without sending the old cursor. Exact request sequence and full unchanged Journal distinguish it from direct resync helper calls; HTTP stream production never runs this browser cursor store. Receive the discriminating foreign-locator check from :277.
test: resumes a retained cursor and resynchronizes from an authorized Snapshot after 409

evidence: An expired cursor whose authorized Snapshot cannot be fetched must return unavailable/resource_unavailable and preserve prior ingest. A successful resync has a real Snapshot and cannot detect treating recovery failure as idle success or advancing the cursor without evidence.
test: does not treat an unrecoverable expired cursor as an empty successful replay

test: refuses a Snapshot whose Scope does not match the Editor Session

evidence: An unknown future Activity kind must reject twice without advancing the retained cursor or stored events, while supported Assistance/Run events remain ingested and manual input remains possible. Real Activity emits only known kinds; reordered known frames cannot catch skipping an unknown event and losing its replay position. The test persists a new edit but does not exercise a rendered editable control.
test: ingests assistance and Run Activity without disabling manual writing or skipping unknown Events

evidence: The replacement-workspace variant holds the same Draft source GET and requires the same absence of Draft Undo records, network mutations and stale callbacks after release. Delete only this parameter; no immediate whole-line saving.
test: Draft Undo respects the editor unmount boundary

evidence: Replacing the live workspace during the held Draft source GET must prevent freezing/submitting old Draft Undo and prevent callbacks or pending-state changes in the successor. A missing workspace dependency/lifetime invalidation can pass a pure unmount case because the editor is destroyed there. Ordinary Undo rate cases do not reach Draft Undo journal freezing.
test: Draft Undo respects the editor replace boundary

test: Draft Undo respects the editor secret boundary

evidence: Changing the Journal schema while Draft source GET is held must prevent freezing any Draft Undo record and send no mutation, with one failure callback. Workspace replacement changes in-memory ownership; secret-field replay fails after a record already exists. Neither exercises schema drift before the freeze transaction.
test: Draft Undo respects the editor schema boundary

evidence: Discard must freeze its complete nonce-free Journal record before Challenge admission, abandon a paused digest when the view changes, and keep response loss unresolved until the exact matching closure event arrives. Repeated stale unresolved observations must not regress a settled record, changed partition must prevent another send, and stored secret contamination must refuse reading. HTTP Discard owns durable database settlement, not IndexedDB freeze/reconciliation or secret-free replay.
test: persists the complete immutable explicit Discard before Admission and only reconciles its exact public event

evidence: Receipt-backed Refused and Conflicted Discard results must both settle the exact Journal decision and clear needs_attention despite the Draft remaining open. The response-loss case reconciles a closed event; treating every open Draft as unresolved would pass that positive closure scenario but fail these terminal refusal/conflict outcomes.
test: keeps exact Receipt-backed refusal and conflict distinct from an infrastructure outcome
